title: Uplift Modelling via Gradient Boosting

problem.claim: Uplift modeling requires a known target for precise computation of the training gradient.

gap.claim: Gradient Boosting has had limited success in uplift modeling, while two-model strategies do not directly address the uplift problem.

narrative_sequence.summary: Gradient Boosting is proficient in complex machine learning tasks but has had limited success in uplift modeling.
Uplift modeling is challenging because precise training-gradient computation requires a known target.
Existing two-model treatment and control strategies have limitations because they do not directly address uplift.

source_observation.claim: Uplift modeling presents a gradient-computation challenge because the target is not known for precise training-gradient calculation.

interpretation.claim: Methods for uplift modeling may need to address the absence of a directly known training target.

application.claim: When adapting gradient-based learning to uplift modeling, explicitly examine how the training gradient is defined and computed.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish which gradient-computation approach is effective.

unknowns: The proposed method is not described.
No empirical results, datasets, baselines, or evaluation metrics are supplied.
The source units do not establish whether the paper introduces a new contribution.
